https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Melons from Japanese PM valued at $200 each, government documents reveal Anthony Albanese’s department confirmed the Japanese crown melons he received from Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, were valued at $200 each, explaining why they weren’t declared on the prime minister’s register of interests. Documents provided to the Senate by Albanese’s assistant minister, Patrick Gorman, reveal official government gift records cataloguing the receipt of four Japanese melons – two handed over directly from Takaichi to Albanese on her visit to Canberra in May, and then another two apparently delivered to The Lodge via the Japanese embassy in June. Each of the four melons was valued at $200, according to the gift documents shared with the Senate. They later, of course, were at the centre of the so-called “melongate” controversy after Albanese’s description of the gift on the Bush Deep podcast. The PM, in the podcast, described the melon gift as “pretty strange but ended up being quite good”

https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-new.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that the United States had given Kyiv information about a number of meetings in Moscow over the last few days."Today we received information from the American side about the meetings in Moscow that took place these days. There were a number of meetings there," Zelenskiy said on Telegram, without going into detail on who was at the meetings."I thank them for the information and for the necessary tone of the conversation with Russia," Zelenskiy added, again without elaborating.The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that CIA Director John Ratcliffe had travelled to Moscow to warn Russia off any attack on a NATO member. The Kremlin dismissed the report, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin would not attack a NATO country, playing down media reports on Ratcliffe's trip.Two sources told Reuters that Ratcliffe had raised the possibility of a Russian operation against a NATO member during the meeting, although it was unclear whether that was the primary purpose of the trip. The talks also covered Russia's support for Iran, one source told Reuters.Also, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Friday that Warsaw was in constant contact with the CIA leadership and was not surprised by Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow."We are not taken by surprise by any information regarding the operations and initiatives the CIA Director is conducting," Tusk told a youth conference when asked if the visit should be a source of concern."Poland was also informed about the need for an urgent discussion on this matter at the highest possible Polish-American level," Tusk added without elaborating.He said that there have been signals in the public domain that Russia is preparing to escalate tensions, both in the war with Ukraine and across the region, and that this autumn and winter are set to be pivotal for Russia.

Photograph: AFF-USA/REX/Shutterstock Jacinda Ardern Jacinda Ardern and husband Clarke Gayford buy $5.3m home in Sydney’s northern beaches Former New Zealand prime minister’s purchase is the highest sale price recorded in suburb of Dee Why this year Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Catie McLeod Tue 22 Sep 2026 04.54 EDT Last modified on Tue 22 Sep 2026 05.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jacinda Ardern and her husband, Clarke Gayford, have bought a $5.3m home in Sydney’s northern beaches, according to a source with knowledge of the sale. The former New Zealand prime minister settled on a home in Dee Why after looking at properties in the area including in nearby Curl Curl. The sale – handled by Raine & Horne Northern Beaches and first reported by the Sydney Morning Herald – is the biggest the suburb has recorded this year, according to the source familiar with the transaction. On a dancefloor at 2am, I heard Jacinda Ardern’s husband say they were moving to Australia. I don’t blame them | Johanna Cosgrove Read more The Guardian has contacted Gayford and a representative for Ardern for comment. In February, Ardern’s office confirmed she was living in Australia , following media reports that she, her husband and their daughter, Neve, had attended open home viewings in Sydney’s northern beaches. “The family has been travelling for a few years now,” a spokesperson from her office told the Guardian at the time. “For the moment they’re basing themselves out of Australia – they have work there, and it brings the added bonus of more time back home in New Zealand .” Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The spokesperson did not elaborate on when the family arrived in Australia nor what kind of work they were doing, but noted it was not unusual for former leaders to spend time overseas after leaving office. Ardern announced her retirement from politics in January 2023, after five years as New Zealand’s prime minister and the leader of the country’s Labour party. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion When she was elected to the top job in October 2017, Ardern became the world’s youngest-serving female leader, aged 37, and later became the second woman to give birth while holding elected office. Since leaving office, Ardern has taken up dual fellowship roles at Harvard University , continued her work on the Christchurch Call – a project she established to combat online extremism after the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings – and joined the board of trustees of Prince William’s Earthshot prize. New Zealand has been grappling with a surge in the number of citizens leaving the country because of a weak economy, high living costs and high unemployment. Many of these people have moved to Australia. https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/.text: Military Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Industry Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links WMD Intelligence Homeland Security Space Military Baiba Braže and Radosław Sikorski discuss strengthening NATO's eastern flank in Ādaži Republic of Latvia - Ministry of Foreign Affairs Published: 09.09.2026. On 9 September 2026, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Baiba Braže, hosted Radosław Sikorski, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Poland, on a working visit. The Ministers visited the Ādaži military base, where Polish soldiers are also serving in the NATO Multinational Brigade. The Ministers discussed the defence of NATO's eastern flank, cooperation between the two countries on border security, support for Ukraine and further pressure on Russia. Baiba Braže expressed her gratitude to Poland for its significant contribution to the security of Latvia and the Baltic region as a whole. Polish soldiers serve in the NATO Multinational Brigade in Latvia, and Poland regularly participates in the Baltic Air Policing mission. The Minister emphasised Latvia's interest in an even greater Polish military presence, particularly in strengthening air defence and airspace surveillance capabilities. The Ministers commended the cooperation between Latvia and Poland in the defence industry. In August this year, a framework agreement was signed for the delivery of several thousand air defence systems to the armed forces of Poland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway. Discussing the security of the eastern border, Baiba Braže emphasised that Latvia and Poland face the instrumentalisation of migrants by Belarus and Russia on a daily basis. The Ministers agreed that strengthening the eastern border should be one of the priorities of the European Union's next Multiannual Financial Framework, with funding allocated for infrastructure, technology, military mobility and the capabilities of the relevant services. The Ministers emphasised the need to continue providing military support to Ukraine, strengthen sanctions against Russia and prevent their circumvention. Baiba Braže stressed that Russia must pay for its aggression and that its frozen assets must be used for Ukraine's defence and reconstruction. The parties also discussed cooperation within the UN and other international organisations to maintain the international isolation of Russia and Belarus.
